claims.text: Reducing grain size in refractory high-entropy nanoalloys increases the fraction of high-energy grain-boundary regions.
Grain-boundary regions introduce heterogeneous atomic-diffusion barriers.
Heterogeneous diffusion barriers impede rapid atomic reordering at high temperatures.
Heterogeneous diffusion barriers impede phase segregation at high temperatures.
Ultrafine- and coarse-grained nanoalloys will be subjected to identical annealing profiles at 800–1000 °C.
Controlling composition, impurities, residual stress, and atmosphere is intended to isolate the effect of grain size.
In situ high-temperature TEM and atom probe tomography will characterize local chemical ordering and grain-boundary segregation.
Differences in local chemical ordering and grain-boundary segregation can be directly attributed to differences in grain-boundary area under the proposed controls.
Smaller grains contain a higher proportion of grain boundaries than coarse grains.
The heterogeneous diffusion-barrier landscape associated with grain boundaries slows atomic-reordering kinetics at high temperature.
Slower atomic-reordering kinetics enhance structural and chemical stability.
Ultrafine-grained nanoalloys will show lower effective diffusion fluxes than coarse-grained nanoalloys at high temperature.
Ultrafine-grained nanoalloys will show reduced phase segregation relative to the coarse-grained baseline.
Ultrafine-grained nanoalloys will show more uniform and kinetically suppressed chemical reordering than the coarse-grained baseline.
The prediction is bounded to annealing at 800–1000 °C in a controlled inert atmosphere with maintained compositional uniformity.
Oxidative conditions or temperatures outside 800–1000 °C may produce behavior that deviates from the prediction.
Impurity segregation and residual stresses may confound the inferred grain-size effect.
A lack of statistically significant reduction in diffusion flux or delay in chemical reordering in ultrafine-grained samples relative to coarse-grained controls would falsify the proposed mechanism.
